Framer AI Agents [...] Hey everyone, I’m Faiz, maker of Quello. 👋 I built Quello because my work was scattered across a dozen tools, and finding a single answer meant opening six tabs and hoping someone had documented it. Quello pulls your tools, files, docs, and knowledge into one searchable workspace. You ask a question and get an answer backed by citations, so you can see exactly where it came from instead of taking it on trust. There’s also a voice agent, so you can just talk to your workspace. You can also write your own docs right inside the workspace. A copilot sits alongside you with the context of your entire workspace, so it can help you document things accurately and carefully, drawing on what’s already there instead of starting from a blank page. The part I’m most excited about is MCP support. Your [...] page. The part I’m most excited about is MCP support. Your work context isn’t locked inside Quello. You can connect it to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Grok, and Perplexity, so whichever AI you use already knows how your work fits together. I built this on my own, so your feedback genuinely shapes what comes next. I’ll be here all day replying to every comment. Thanks for checking it out!

Review Rambox?

Reviewers mostly see Rambox as a practical hub for juggling many messaging, email, and web apps in one place, with tabs, shortcuts, workspaces, custom apps, and broad support across Linux, Mac, and Windows. They praise its stability, frequent updates, clean interface, and generous free tier, saying it reduces clutter and makes multitasking easier. The main complaints are performance on lower-memory machines, energy use, latency when waking apps, limited extension support, some custom app glitches, repeated upsell prompts, and a few missing touches like menu bar access, Spanish, and better credential tools.

Review Rambox?

Reviewers mostly see Rambox as a practical way to keep messaging, email, and other everyday apps in one place, helping cut window clutter and making multitasking easier. Users praise its stability, cross-platform support, tabs, shortcuts, workspace organization, and a polished interface, with several noting long-term reliability and useful updates. The main complaints are resource use and speed on weaker machines, some latency when waking apps, limited extension support, issues with certain custom apps, frequent upgrade prompts, and a few missing conveniences like menu bar access, Spanish language support, and better password-manager integration.
